newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Costello says wage ruling is not inflation threat.
newsitem.headline: Costello says wage ruling is not inflation threat.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said Tuesday's wage increase granted by the Australian Industrial Relations Commission would not threaten the nation's inflation outlook.

"The living wage decision --- if the ACTU (Australian Council of Trade Unions) claims had been granted -- would have threatened our inflation prospects," Costello said at a news conference to comment on the March quarter inflation data.
"The good thing about yesterday's decision is that that decision won't threaten our inflation prospects, that is the good thing," he said.
"But the thing that we have to be mindful of and careful of on the wages front is enterprise bargains," he said.

"The enterprise bargains are running well in advance of award adjustments and it is very important in relation to those enterprise bargains that they are consistent with an overall wages outcome as the RBA (Reserve Bank of Australia) targets."

The national labour tribunal on Tuesday announced a A$10 per week pay rise for lower paid workers in contrast to the government's support for an A$8 rise and the union movement's claim for a A$20 weekly rise.
